answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Proof of work on a memory-hard function changes that arithmetic: a memory-hard puzzle that GPUs cannot speed up, so the vertex for each fake is paid in the real world. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the vine is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the wander of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
